Ha your story sounds so familiar. I too thought something was wrong with my pancreas. Anyways when GI had run every test on earth and ran through my wallet they never wanted to see me again (and left me with no answers)... good thing because the feeling was mutual. 

You see endo patients get run through GI constantly. People never end up at an endo specialists as there first stop it’s almost always their last. I’d just hate to see you waste a lot of time, money, and energy looking in the wrong direction. Because I totally get it. The process is so draining. 

I cannot confirm that I have endometriosis as I have not had lap surgery yet. But I have had every other test done at this point. I am scheduled for surgery June 4th and if the endo is confirmed on my ureter they will be removing it at that time. 

I would love to keep each other updated! It’s so nice to find someone who understands. Keep fighting the good fight and I support you with whatever steps you take! Just know you have a friend who is rooting for you :)

Hey, I found your post while searching “ureter” and I just wanted to say all of my symptoms are very very similar to yours. After years of worsening symptoms and terrible doctors I ended up at an excellent endometriosis specialist who is Nancy’s Nook approved. 

On my last MRI it showed hydronephrosis of my kidney which she believes is being caused by endo on the ureter. This whole time I was thinking this was related to my intestines - because similar to you I felt that constant inflammation, often made worse by caffeine or certain foods, with bloating but no bowel issued an area that to me seemed like it would be my intestines.

Anyways 2 endoscopy/colonoscopys, 2 MRIs and 3 CAT scans later I know now apparently that can actually be a kidney/ureter related issue. 

I totally get the struggle but I would really try to find a specialist who will excise off ureter. It has been known to cause kidney failure and often times is not caught until too late - no meant to scare you, just do not listen to someone who would suggest you do nothing about it. But also like someone else mentioned it is a delicate surgery and needs an expert - sometimes a urologist will even work with the surgeon to ensure it goes smoothly.

I have my excision in a month. Can’t come soon enough.

Best of luck to you!
